findings.title: Redis::purge() on rebuild unsets the cached connection but does not close the discarded socket; note GC/destruct handling
findings.problem: Verified Illuminate\Redis\RedisManager::purge($name) is only unset($this->connections[$name]); it removes the manager's cached reference but does not call disconnect()/close() on the previous Connection/raw client. In the design's closure the old $connection/$client are overwritten by the rebuilt pair, so the previous objects become unreferenced and phpredis closes the socket on __destruct. Correct in practice, but on an idle connection the rebuild runs ~once per OPT_READ_TIMEOUT second, so for a brief window two sockets can coexist until GC runs. The design asserts a 'clean new socket' without stating the old socket is released by destruct rather than by an explicit close.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to §6.2: Redis::purge() only drops the cached reference; the old connection's socket is closed when the prior Connection/raw client is no longer referenced (phpredis destruct); no explicit close() is needed on the rebuild path because $connection/$client are immediately overwritten, and finally still closes the last active socket once. Optionally, for determinism, call try { $client->close(); } catch (\Throwable) {} immediately before Redis::purge() when $client is already set.
